proposals.name: Orlania
proposals.entry:
Type: Lost Nation
Region: Sayir Sea
Capital: Orlan
Status: Destroyed during the Hundred Kingdom Wars
People: Orlanians

Orlania was a rugged island nation of the Sayir Sea, remembered for its sailors, mercenary soldiers, metalworkers, and a cultural stubbornness that its neighbors alternately admired and found exhausting.

Its people were distinctive for their great lower tusks and elaborate blue-black tattooing. Orlanian tattoos could record family, profession, military service, marriage, mourning, religious devotion, great journeys, and personal vows. An elderly Orlanian might carry something approaching a biography across their skin.

The Iron Islands

Orlania was never particularly rich in farmland. Its wealth came from the sea and from what lay beneath its rocky islands.

The country exported iron, copper, worked steel, ship fittings, preserved fish, lamp oil, heavy rope, and weapons. Orlanian armorers were particularly respected. Their work favored durability over elegance, and surviving Orlanian military equipment remains valuable throughout the Sayir Sea.

Orlania also exported soldiers.

For generations, Orlanian companies served as marines, guards, engineers, and mercenaries throughout the Hundred Kingdoms. This produced a strange nation where fishermen might understand siegecraft and village blacksmiths could recognize the uniforms of six foreign armies.

The Hundred Kingdom Wars

Orlania entered the war gradually.

At first it sold weapons, ships, and soldiers to several combatants while officially maintaining neutrality. As alliances hardened, this became increasingly impossible.

Orlanian ships were attacked.

Orlanian mercenaries found themselves fighting one another under foreign banners.

Then Trovus demanded access to Orlanian harbors and military facilities.

Orlania refused.

The refusal transformed an inconvenient neutral nation into an enemy.

The Destruction of Orlania

The resulting Trovian invasion of Orlania was expected to last weeks.

It lasted years.

The Orlanians turned their islands into fortresses, fighting from harbors, mines, villages, sea caves, and mountain roads. Trovus eventually abandoned the idea of conquering a useful Orlania and instead decided to make continued resistance impossible.

Ports were bombarded.

Mines were collapsed.

Fishing fleets were burned.

Freshwater works were destroyed.

Several smaller islands were almost completely depopulated.

The capital, Orlan, finally fell after a prolonged siege. Much of it burned, and portions of the old harbor district reportedly slid into the sea during the bombardment.

Trovus technically won.

There was simply very little left to govern.

Orlanians Today

Orlania no longer exists as a functioning nation.

Its surviving people are scattered throughout the Sayir Sea and beyond: sailors, refugees, laborers, mercenaries, smiths, criminals, and old soldiers who still describe themselves as Orlanian despite possessing no country to return to.

Some preserve the language and tattoo traditions carefully.

Others refuse to speak of the islands at all.

In Fogport, the most infamous surviving Orlanian is Harlok Yix, the enormous veteran and murderer known throughout the Shambles as the Shambles Butcher.

There remains one particularly dangerous disagreement among surviving Orlanians:

Whether Orlania is dead—or merely occupied.
